guideTitle: 6 Best Ratchet Loppers for Heavy Duty Pruning in 2026
metaTitle: Best Ratchet Loppers for Heavy Duty Cuts 2026
metaDescription: Six heavy duty ratchet loppers compared on cutting capacity, handle length, bypass versus anvil blades and ease of use for lower hand strength.
introParagraphs: Loppers exist for the branches that hand pruners cannot touch, and ratchet loppers add a second advantage: they cut in stages, so thick wood does not demand one huge pull on the handles. For gardeners with less arm or grip strength, that is the difference between finishing a pruning job and giving up halfway.

This guide compares six ratchet loppers: the EZ Kut G2 42-inch extendable anvil lopper, the Kings County Tools bypass lopper and its bypass-and-anvil set, the GARTOL four-step anvil lopper, the Fiskars 32 inch Ratchet Drive anvil lopper, and the Kimura Pro anvil lopper. We evaluated them on cutting capacity, reach, blade type and how the ratchet helps with thick branches.

Ratchet pruners sold for one hand are a different tool and are left out, as are non-ratchet bypass loppers such as the Fiskars PowerGear2. A ratchet lopper earns its place when you cut branches an inch or more across and would otherwise reach for a saw.

products.name: EZ Kut G2 Ratcheting Anvil Loppers 42 Inch
products.description:
The EZ Kut G2 is a heavy duty anvil lopper with a six-stage ratcheting mechanism that multiplies force on every squeeze. It cuts branches up to 1.5 inches thick, and the handles telescope out to 42 inches for extra reach and leverage. The listing describes lightweight aluminum handles that lock securely, with an anti-slip cushion grip and shock absorbing pads.

Six stages is the most ratchet steps in this lineup, so each squeeze moves the blade a short distance and thick wood demands less force per squeeze. The tradeoff is time, because a full 1.5 inch cut takes many clicks. As an anvil blade it works best on dead and dry wood, because it crushes rather than slices, although the maker also says it handles green branches. The 1.5 inch ceiling is also the lowest of the group.

On the ownership side, the 42 inch extension gives reach for overhead limbs without a ladder in many cases, but a fully extended lopper is awkward in tight shrubs, so collapse it for low work. Check the locks every time you change length. Compared with the 2 inch Fiskars Ratchet Drive it gives up half an inch of capacity, and compared with the Kings County bypass lopper at 26 to 40 inches it reaches farther and ratchets more aggressively, while the Kings County is better for live green growth.
products.bestFor: Gardeners cutting thick dead or dry branches with limited hand strength.
pros: Six-stage ratchet lowers force per squeeze

products.name: Kings County Tools Double Ratcheting Bypass Loppers
products.description:
The Kings County bypass lopper pairs a double ratcheting mechanism with scissor-style bypass blades, which are better suited to green wood. The telescoping handles run from 26 to 40 inches with six pin-locked position stops and rubber grips. The listing gives a 2 inch jaw capacity, an alloy steel and rubber build, and a weight of 3.99 pounds.

Bypass blades cut like scissors, so live branches are cut cleanly and heal better. Combined with a double ratchet, they bring thick green wood within reach of weaker hands. The cost is that bypass blades usually need more force than anvil blades on the same branch, partly offsetting the ratchet advantage. At 26 inches long when closed it is also bulkier to store than a hand pruner.

In practice the pin-locked positions let you set a length for the job, and the shorter 26 inch setting is easier to control in tight areas. Make sure the pin is fully seated before you cut. Compared with the EZ Kut G2 you give up two inches of maximum reach but gain a blade that is kinder to live branches and half an inch more rated capacity. Against the Kings County set it carries only the bypass blade, so deadwood is better handled by the anvil version.
products.bestFor: Gardeners pruning live green branches who want clean cuts and adjustable reach.
pros: Bypass blades cut live wood cleanly
26 to 40 inch handles with six locked stops
cons: Bypass needs more force than anvil
Shorter maximum reach than the EZ Kut G2
Pin locks must be fully engaged

products.name: Kings County Tools Bypass Loppers and Anvil Pruner Set
products.description:
This Kings County set covers both wood types by including a bypass lopper for green wood and an anvil lopper for dry wood. Both use an oversized double ratcheting mechanism with a stated cutting jaw capacity of 2 to 2.5 inches. The anvil lopper is described for dry wood, kindling and dead branches, and both tools have 26 to 40 inch telescoping handles with six pin-locked stops and rubber grips.

Having both blades in one set is the main advantage. You can cut live branches cleanly with the bypass and break through dead wood with the anvil, without compromising on either. The set matches the GARTOL at the top of the capacity range and is a half inch above the 2 inch Fiskars Ratchet Drive and Kimura, well ahead of the EZ Kut G2 at 1.5 inches. The cost is that you buy two long tools.

Ownership means storing two loppers, which takes more room than one, and cleaning and oiling two sets of blades and ratchets. Per the dimensions listed, the bypass lopper is 26 inches long and the anvil lopper is 26 inches with a slightly taller head. Compared with the single Kings County bypass lopper it adds an anvil tool for dead limbs. It is the best fit for a yard with both live trees and dead wood, while a one-wood-type yard is better served by a single lopper.
products.bestFor: Gardeners with both live trees and dead wood to cut who want the largest capacity.
pros: Bypass and anvil blades for both wood types
2 to 2.5 inch capacity, among the largest here
cons: Two tools take more storage room
More weight to carry than a single tool
More than needed if you cut one wood type

products.name: GARTOL Heavy-Duty Extendable Ratchet Loppers 28 to 41 Inch
specs: Cuts up to 2.5 inch dry wood
products.description:
The GARTOL is an anvil lopper with a four-step ratchet system rated for dry branches up to 2.5 inches in diameter. The aluminum handles extend from 28 to 41 inches, and the blade is heat-treated high carbon steel. Soft TPR grips are designed to stay secure during longer sessions.

It matches the Kings County set for the top capacity in this guide while being a single tool, which is a real advantage if you cut mostly dead wood and hardwood. Four steps sits between the EZ Kut G2 at six and the Kings County double ratchet in complexity. The tradeoff is the anvil blade, which crushes rather than slices, so it is a poor choice for the live branches you want to heal cleanly.

For ownership, aluminum handles keep carrying weight down, and the telescoping lock needs to be checked before every cut. Wipe the blade after sappy work and store it closed. Compared with the EZ Kut G2 it extends 1 inch shorter at 41 inches but cuts a full inch thicker on paper. Compared with the Kimura Pro, which is rated for 2 inches, it adds half an inch of capacity and a longer maximum reach of 41 inches versus 37.
products.bestFor: Cutting thick dead limbs with the longest rated capacity in a single tool.
pros: Cuts up to 2.5 inch dry wood

products.name: Fiskars 32 Inch Ratchet Drive Garden Anvil Loppers
products.description:
The Fiskars Ratchet Drive lopper is a fixed 32 inch anvil tool rated for 2 inch dry, dead branches. The ratchet compounds force with a series of easy squeezes, and the fully hardened, precision-ground steel blade carries a low-friction coating that resists sap gumming and rust. The handles are riveted steel for lasting value.

It is the simplest tool here, because the handle length is fixed with no telescoping pins to fail or forget. That also makes it lighter in concept and quicker to grab for a quick cleanup. The tradeoff is reach, since 32 inches is the shortest in the lineup, and the anvil style is meant for thick, dry, dead branches, not for clean live pruning.

Ownership is easy: wipe the coated blade, oil the pivot and ratchet, and store it closed. A well-known maker also means blades and parts are easier to find. Compared with the EZ Kut G2 it has 10 fewer inches of maximum reach but half an inch more rated capacity. Compared with the Kimura Pro, which collapses to 25 inches and extends to 37, the Fiskars is simpler but cannot adjust.
products.bestFor: Dead branch cleanup with a simple fixed-length tool from an established maker.
pros: Fixed length, no pins to loosen
cons: Anvil blade is for dry wood

products.name: Kimura Pro Heavy Duty Ratchet Anvil Loppers 25 to 37 Inch
products.description:
The Kimura Pro is an anvil lopper with a ratchet mechanism the maker says multiplies power by up to 5 times, for branches up to 2 inches thick. Easy-twist locks extend the lightweight aluminum handles from 25 to 37 inches. The Japanese SK5 steel anvil blade carries a PTFE coating to resist sap build-up and rust, and soft TPR grips aid control.

Twist locks avoid fiddly pins, which is easier on arthritic fingers than pulling a pin. The weight is described as evenly distributed between the blades and handles, so the head does not feel heavy at full extension. The tradeoff is that 5X is a maker claim, not a measurement, and the shorter 37 inch extension reaches 4 inches less than the EZ Kut G2. As an anvil lopper it crushes live wood.

For ownership, wipe the coated blade and check the twist locks before heavy cuts. Compared with the GARTOL, which cuts 2.5 inches and extends to 41, the Kimura gives up half an inch and 4 inches of reach for a lighter feel. Compared with the Fiskars Ratchet Drive at a fixed 32 inches, it adds telescoping and a stronger leverage claim.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want twist-lock handles and a strong leverage claim.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity tells you the thickest branch the lopper is rated to cut, and it is a ceiling for dry soft wood, not a daily target. The EZ Kut G2 is rated for 1.5 inches, the Kings County bypass, Fiskars Ratchet Drive and Kimura Pro for 2 inches, and the Kings County set and GARTOL for 2 to 2.5 inches. Stay half an inch below the rating on hardwood to protect the mechanism. Pick a capacity at least half an inch above your typical branch.

Bypass blades slice like scissors and suit live green wood, while anvil blades crush against a flat block and suit dead, dry wood. The Kings County bypass lopper is bypass, the EZ Kut G2, Fiskars, GARTOL and Kimura are anvil, and the Kings County set includes both. A crushed live stem heals slowly and invites rot. Match the blade to the wood you cut most to get cleaner cuts and less effort.

More stages mean a lighter squeeze but more clicks. The EZ Kut G2 has six stages, the GARTOL has four, and the Kings County models use a double ratcheting mechanism. The Kimura claims up to 5X power, though that is a maker figure. If strength is the issue, a six-stage tool is easier on the hands, and if speed matters, fewer stages with long handles may be enough.

Longer handles give more reach and leverage but are harder to control. The EZ Kut G2 extends to 42 inches, the GARTOL to 41, the Kings County to 40, the Kimura to 37 and the Fiskars is fixed at 32. Use the short setting in tight spaces and the long one for overhead cuts. Check that lock pins or twist locks fully seat before you cut.

Long ratchet loppers are heavier than hand pruners, and overhead cuts exaggerate the weight. Only the Kings County bypass lopper states a weight, 3.99 pounds, while the other listings mention lightweight aluminum handles without numbers. The two-tool Kings County set will be the heaviest load to carry, and a single lopper is easier for long sessions. If you have shoulder trouble, favor a telescoping model like the 28 to 41 inch GARTOL and shorten it for low work to keep the head close to your body.

Cushioned grips and anti-slip surfaces matter because loppers use both hands and sweaty palms. The EZ Kut G2 has an anti-slip cushion handle, the Kings County uses rubber grips with pin-locked stops, and the Kimura and GARTOL use soft TPR with twist or pin adjustment. If your fingers are stiff, a twist lock is easier than pulling a pin. Wear snug work gloves to improve the grip further.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated jaw capacity: 1.5 inches on the EZ Kut G2, 2 inches on the Kings County bypass, Fiskars and Kimura, and 2 to 2.5 inches on the Kings County set and GARTOL. The lineup leader on rated capacity is the GARTOL as a single tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bypass blades on the Kings County lopper, anvil on the EZ Kut G2, GARTOL, Fiskars and Kimura, and both in the Kings County set. Blade type decides which wood each tool handles best, so it shaped our badges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ratchet leverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the six-stage ratchet on the EZ Kut G2, the four-step system on the GARTOL, the double ratcheting on the Kings County tools and the 5X claim on the Kimura. More stages reduce force per squeeze, so we weighted that for users with limited strength.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated handle lengths: 42 inches extendable on the EZ Kut G2, 28 to 41 on the GARTOL, 26 to 40 on the Kings County lopper, 25 to 37 on the Kimura and fixed 32 on the Fiskars.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the cushion grips on the EZ Kut G2, the rubber grips on the Kings County, and the TPR grips on the GARTOL and Kimura. Slip resistance matters for loppers because they take two hands and a lot of force.

faq.q: Which ratchet lopper is best for thick branches?
faq.a: The GARTOL and the Kings County set list a cutting capacity of 2 to 2.5 inches, the largest here. The EZ Kut G2 is rated for 1.5 inches and offers six ratchet stages. Choose by branch size and wood type, and remember the maximum is a ceiling for dry wood.

faq.q: Bypass or anvil loppers for live branches?
faq.a: Bypass blades cut live wood cleanly and help the plant heal. Anvil loppers crush the branch and are better on dead wood. The Kings County bypass lopper is the match for green branches, and the Kings County set includes both blade types.

faq.q: Does a ratchet lopper really reduce effort?
faq.a: Yes, a ratchet divides one hard pull into several lighter squeezes. The EZ Kut G2 has six stages, the GARTOL four and the Kings County tools use double ratcheting. The tradeoff is more clicks per cut, so a thick branch takes longer.

Longer handles give more reach and leverage but are harder to control. The EZ Kut G2 extends to 42 inches, the Kings County lopper runs 26 to 40, and the Fiskars is fixed at 32. Use the shorter setting in tight spaces and for accuracy.

Telescoping loppers rely on pins or twist locks to hold the length. If a lock is not fully engaged, the handle can slide during a cut and pinch a hand. Check the locks every time you change length, and note that the Fiskars avoids the issue with fixed handles.

faq.q: How do I maintain ratchet loppers?
faq.a: Clean sap from the blade, dry the tool, and add light oil to the pivot and ratchet. Coated blades such as the Fiskars and Kimura wipe clean more easily. Store them closed and dry, and avoid cutting wire or wood beyond the rating, which can chip an anvil blade.

faq.q: Can I use loppers on branches over their rated size?
faq.a: No. Cutting beyond capacity can damage the ratchet and is hard on your hands. For thicker wood, switch to a pruning saw. If you often meet 2.5 inch limbs, choose a lopper like the GARTOL with room to spare.
